reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) directly supports dynamic recrystallization and precipitation raising activation energy in a single-phase CoCrFeNiMn HEA, but it does not address FCC/BCC multilayers, interfaces, or whether these processes localize at interfaces and govern creep in that geometry. The extrapolation from bulk single-phase to interface-dominated multilayer behavior is a key gap.
premises: Dynamic recrystallization and precipitation occur in CoCrFeNiMn HEA at high stress/temperature
These processes raise creep activation energy (e.g., from ~268 to ~380 kJ/mol) and stress exponent
The same dynamic microstructural evolution will occur at interfaces in FCC/BCC HEA multilayers
Interface-localized precipitates and recrystallized grains act as additional dislocation obstacles
The mechanism shifts creep from dislocation climb to a combined climb + recrystallization/precipitation regime
